newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus insurance companies plan expansions.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus insurance companies plan expansions.

text.p: Cyprus insurance company Paneuropean plans to expand into reinsurance, while its subsidiary Interamerican plans to branch into mutual funds, officials of the company said on Monday.

"In cooperation with large overseas reinsures the (Paneuropean) Group will develop in the near future specialised activities in the area of reinsurance," executive chairman Nicos Shakolas told shareholders at the group's annual meeting in Nicosia.
Paneuropean is the holding company of Interamerican Insurance, Philiki Insurance, Euroinvestment and Finance and Philoktimatiki Ltd.
It sold its life and general insurance portfolios to Interamerican and Philiki insurances in 1996.
Shakolas said the Paneuropean group premiums rose to 41.4 million pounds ($79.7 million) in 1996 from 19.2 million pounds in 1995, establishing Paneuropean as the largest insurance group in Cyprus.
Consolidated pre-tax profits of the group were 2.4 million pounds from 3.9 million in 1995. The meeting approved a 20 percent or 10 cents per share, dividend to shareholders.

Interamerican, one of the largest life insurance companies in Cyprus, reported pre-tax profit of 2.24 million pounds over 1.24 million in 1995. In 1996 the life insurance portfolios of Philiki and Paneuropean were transferred to Interamerican.
Interamerican's general insurance portfolio was sold to Philiki in January 1996.

Shakolas said Interamerican will participate in the establishment of a mutual fund company with investors from Cyprus and abroad in a fresh attempt to create better investment opportunities and to strengthen the capital market.
The board approved a 20 percent, or 10 cent per share dividend to shareholders.

Philiki, which specialises in general insurance, posted pre-tax profits of 4.6 million in 1996 from 1.6 million in 1995. It is paying a 12 percent dividend, at 6 cent per share, in addition to the interim dividend of 12 percent already paid.

The company plans to increase its share capital to 15 million ordinary shares with a nominal value of 50 cents from 10 million shares of 50 cents. It will also issue bonus shares at a ratio of one for every one held to shareholders registered on June 20 1997.
Philiki will proceed with a rights issue of new ordinary shares at a ratio of 1 to 12 held to all shareholders registered on the company register as at June 21 1997.
All three companies are introducing share incentive schemes for staff, Shakolas said. ($0.519 pounds)
